solarEruptions.source: NASA DONKI / Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office · experimental WSA-ENLIL forecasts

entries.note: A faint loop CME seen to the NW in early GOES CCOR-1 imagery and in SOHO LASCO C3 (after the data gap). It is fully covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. No source has been found for this CME in EUV imagery, so it is likely far-sided.

Faint minor CME seen to the NE CCOR-1 and in a couple early timestamps of LASCO C3. It is possibly seen very faintly in a few SOHO LASCO C2 images and covered by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. | No source has been found, so it is likely far sided.

Minor CME faintly seen to the NE in early timestamps of SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 (which had several bad images around the time). | No clear source have been found for this CME. There are continuously moving field lines seen close to/behind the NE limb in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284, which could be indication of a far-sided source.

CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap. The potential source may be an eruption faintly seen beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting at approximately 2026-11-20T10:20Z. Moving/opening field lines are also faintly seen beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA.
Faint CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery only. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is not found and is likely farsided.

Faint CME observed to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3, too faint in LASCO C2 and ongoing STEREO A COR2 data gap, and is observed more clearly as it travels further out of the field-of-view. No distinct source is observed for this CME.

Narrow CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery starting at 2026-11-19T13:38Z. The potential source is a filament eruption seen centered around S25E70 as best seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. Filament liftoff can be seen starting in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-11-19T14:12Z.
This CME is faintly visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. This CME is not clearly visible in other coronagraph imagery. No source is found in available EUV imagery.

CME seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME can also be faintly seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 before a real-time data gap starting at 2026-11-19T09:48Z. The source is likely an eruption from west of Active Region 14579, located around N15E10, starting at 2026-11-19T07:09Z as seen in SDO AIA 304/193 imagery. Dimming can be best seen in SDO AIA 193 and an ejecta of material is visible in SDO AIA 304. The eruption is also visible near the east limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery.

CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-18T16:38Z to 2026-11-19T02:09Z. The source of this event is a slow erupting prominence seen originating from beyond the West limb in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. This prominence begins to become unstable at approximately 2026-11-18T04:15Z, but does not appear to fully erupt from the disk until approximately 2026-11-18T18:44Z. Field line opening can also be seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

CME first seen to the SW by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-11-18T21:15Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a data gap from 2026-11-18T19:00Z to 2026-11-18T23:12Z, or STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-18T16:38Z. The source of this event is likely beyond the SW limb and can be seen as field line movement/opening in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-11-18T19:48Z.

Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-18T16:00Z. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in C2 and is there for not visible in other coronagraphs. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen originating from Active Region 14581 (S10E56) beginning at approx. 20206-11-18T10:54Z as seen as dimming and field line opening in SDO AIA 193.

This CME is visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-18T07:53Z to 2026-11-18T11:09Z. The CME may also be visible to the west in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3, but is overlapping in the field of view with the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-11-18T02:00Z. The source may be part of the eruption seen near disk center in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery, potentially centered around S05W90 starting around 2026-11-18T03:55Z with moving field lines and minor dimming observed.
Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is not found in available EUV imagery.

CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around N10W80. The eruption starts around 2026-11-18T00:52Z as seen as moving field lines near the west limb in GOES SUVI 284/304 and SDO AIA 193 imagery. Post-eruption dimming can also be seen in STEREO A EUV 195 following a data gap from 2026-11-17T21:05Z to 2026-11-18T01:55Z.

Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and faintly in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery and may be obscured by a data gap from 2026-11-17T20:53Z to 2026-11-18T02:38Z. The source is not clear but may be an eruption beyond the NE limb as seen from SDO and GOES. An eruption starting around 2026-11-18T01:40Z can be seen beyond the east limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery, but timing-wise this may not be the best candidate source.

CME first seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-11-17T22:30Z. It is covered by real-time data gaps in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is likely associated with an M1.7 class flare from 14578 (S12W71) which peaked at 2026-11-17T21:39Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131 accompanied by some westward directed ejecta best seen in SDO AIA 304.

Narrow CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-11-17T20:30Z. It is also seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely related to a filament eruption from AR 14579 (N15E36) beginning around 2026-11-17T19:01Z best seen in SDO AIA 304. The ejecta appears to be directed northeastward.

CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-11-17T19:53Z. It is also seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely far-sided and possibly related to some very faint field line movement seen well beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-11-17T18:00Z. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is an M1.1 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W68) seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T15:45Z.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and related to a filament eruption visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T06:20Z. An opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb at this time in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery as well.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a C2.0 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W61) seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T04:51Z.

CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-11-16T21:48Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C3, or in later frames in SOHO LASCO C2 in real time due to data gaps. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption from AR 14578 (S12W58) beginning around 2026-11-16T21:18Z best seen in SDO AIA 304 as westward directed ejecta.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a C2.2 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W52) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-16T16:00Z.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W51) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-16T14:54Z.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a C2.3 flare from Active Region 14578 (S12W50) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-16T11:30Z.

This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption centered at approximately S15W155 as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-15T18:00Z.

This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth or STEREO-facing disk around the time of this event.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to a far-sided filament eruption observed over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery which lifts-off around 2026-11-15T08:00Z.

This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth or STEREO-facing disk around the time of this event.

Bright CME with a narrower brighter bulk and a wider fainter shock seen to the NE in CCOR-1. Its source is an elongated, fast developing filament eruption from close to the NE limb ~(N17E70) starting at 2026-11-14T21:17Z and seemingly deflecting northward. There is an associated relatively long duration C2.8 flare originating near AR 14579 (N17E72) and peaking at 2026-11-14T21:27Z, as well as a type II burst. The long erupting filament is best seen in GOES SUVI 304/284 imagery but also seen in SDO AIA 304/131/171, with an EUV wave seen clearly in AIA 193.

A loop CME seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. It overlaps with the 2026-11-14T14:00Z CME and seems faster than it, so it possibly catches up with it. No clear source has been found for this CME, so it is likely far-sided.
